operations.comment: ; Readability pass: fixed CPU PRG view [0,1,2,3], mapper 3 / CNROM.
; Physical storage = CPU alias - $8000 + $10 for PRG only.
; RAM/PPU/OAM/palette spaces remain separate; zero-page scratch is reused by modes.
; OamShadow contains four-byte NES sprites: Y, tile, attributes, X.
; PaletteShadow holds 32 palette bytes; TileStripShadow is reversed transfer order.
; Parsed iNES header independently establishes mapper 3, 32 KiB PRG and 32 KiB CHR boundaries.
; Printable ASCII title/revision/build credit immediately precedes validated Reset entry at file 0x43;
; exact extent checked against bytes.
; Wait for two vblanks before disabling rendering. Clear CPU RAM, seed the random state, then run
; title/map/street and bonus modes. CNROM fixes PRG slots to physical banks [0,1,2,3]. The stack
; begins at $0180; NMI uses a RAM-selected handler.
; Reset score, lives and route state before returning to map selection. Numeric score fields hold
; ASCII digits, not binary decimal values.
; Restore the route display, then initialize the next street segment.
; Initialize route selection and player state. Mainline waits here while NMI owns frame updates.
; Service deferred audio while NMI advances street play. The street-active latch and failure flag
; select the next transition.
; Failure consumes a life after the transition delay; restart at the map while lives remain.
; A cleared street-active latch ends the street. Commit route progress, award distance bonus and
; dispatch the selected bonus mode.
; Selectors $81/$82/$83 choose cafe, school and dance. Other negative selectors enter driving. The
; bonus result in $a9 controls the success/failure cards.
; Enter school after its introductory card. Failure consumes a life; success and failure both return
; through route progression.
; Enter dance after its introductory card; use its result latch to choose the following card.
; Run driving and show its result card. A bounded direct entry now demonstrates the initialized road,
; car and HUD; natural success and the complete caller-return transition remain unresolved.
; Show the game-over card, then reset the game counters.
; A is the frame count. NMI decrements FrameDelay; keep servicing deferred audio until it reaches
; zero. Requires an installed NMI handler and enabled NMI.
; Disable NMI and clear street update gates, pause, scrolling and failure state before mode
; initialization.
; Clear street subsystems before a transition and hide/reset the object pool.
; Disable rendering, unpack the title display, install TitleNmi and select CHR bank 3. Wait for a
; fresh button press while stirring the random seed; blank the display on exit.
; Preserve A/X/Y, delay for the title raster split, service display/palette/controller/audio, then restore registers and return from NMI.
; Display the completion figure through the shared two-sprite drawing helper, then wait and fade
; between modes.
; If the player used the raised movement state, convert half the vertical offset through a capped
; digit lookup into hundreds of score. Display the three digits briefly, add them to the ASCII score
; and check records/extra life.
; Build the street background, HUD and palettes; install StreetNmi. Display lives and blink the player
; before enabling normal movement. Scroll coordinates are pipelined by two frames.
; NMI jumps through the RAM handler pointer. Every installed handler preserves A/X/Y and returns with
; RTI.
; IRQ is unused by this fixed-PRG CNROM program; return immediately.
; Bounded increasing lookup bytes 1,1,2..9; preceding IRQ RTI and following routine boundary
; inspected.
; NMI sets the audio-pending latch. Mainline drains it once through the audio engine and clears it.
; A selects one of the small bus-conflict-safe values in the table. Write back the ROM byte at the
; same address, selecting a CNROM CHR bank without changing PRG mapping.
; Eight-entry increasing 0..7 table between decoded routines.
; Mix three persistent bytes by shifts/XOR and rotate the result through the seed. A is also returned
; as a small pseudo-random source; no statistical quality is assumed.
; Eight single-bit masks followed by repeated four-byte NES palette groups with universal backdrop 0F;
; neighboring controller and screen code inspected.
; When active and unpaused, derive direction from the low controller nibble, choose velocity and
; compute candidate position. Build four tile probes from candidate coordinates and camera scroll.
; For each corner, split pixel coordinates into tile and sub-tile parts. Fold vertical wrap and
; nametable selection into four PPU address pairs.
; Select one of the direction-indexed signed fixed-point velocity tables. Override direction/table
; when the special movement latch is set. Store X/Y fractional and integer steps.
; Read eight PPU tile samples through four player and four additional address pairs. Each PPUDATA
; access discards the buffered first read. Mark collision samples ready.
; Gate on active, unpaused and ready samples. Direction selects corner order; tile properties provide
; a high-bit flag and indirect collision response. Unhandled tiles permit normal movement.
; Apply signed fractional position deltas, clamp X to $05..$f0 and Y to $1e..$a8, and advance the
; scroll-speed history. A blocked state can zero both velocity pairs.
; Derive animation from movement direction/state. A changed animation reloads its script; the script
; dispatch table selects handlers. Integrate signed vertical offset and emit the player four-sprite
; rectangle plus optional two-sprite attachment.
; Count down the frame duration; at zero, fetch a script opcode and jump through its handler table.
; Script extent and unvisited handlers remain redirect questions.
; Sign-extend the one-byte acceleration and integrate velocity/offset. Clamp against the stored
; baseline while descending, then project coordinates into OAM.
; Write the four player sprite coordinates from world position minus vertical offset. Optionally
; position the two attachment sprites, hiding overflow.
; Read frame index and duration from the animation script. Expand the frame into four tile numbers,
; clear sprite attributes, save the next cursor and resume vertical integration.
; Read a script address low byte and convert it to a cursor relative to the script base; redispatch immediately.
; Consume one loop-count byte and continue at the next player command.
; Decrement the saved count; branch to the encoded script address while nonzero, otherwise skip that operand.
; Clear the raised state and vertical motion, set a five-tick action cooldown and invalidate the previous animation so the normal update reloads it.
; Start the scripted vertical arc using negative acceleration and a positive initial velocity; advance
; the script cursor.
; Read the attachment enable flag. Initialize its two tiles/attributes or hide them, then resume the
; animation interpreter.
; Advance the script cursor, request the route-boundary reposition sequence and disable player updates before returning to sprite projection.
; Advance the cursor, increment the street failure latch and disable player updates. The main loop handles the failure transition.
; Clear the collision-motion flag, apply the shared player hit transition and resume collision processing.
; When neither attached nor already moving, copy the scripted direction into motion state and latch it active.
; Clear the movement override and vertical baseline before normal collision resolution.
; Clear collision motion; tile-state values at least four request animation 4 before rejoining the collision loop.
; Clear collision motion; apply the shared hit transition only when the equipment/state selector is nonzero.
; Count six blinking intervals, alternating the player sprite positions and hidden Y values. Pause
; freezes this entry effect; clear its active latch when finished.
; Scan the current route data until one of two packed edge descriptors matches the route row. Derive
; player coordinates from its nibbles, reset vertical state and update sprites.
; Initialize player position and animation, clear velocities/offsets and collision latches. Negative
; probe high bytes mark samples unavailable until rebuilt.

; Ignore an inactive player, and defer ordinary hits while attached. Forced hits bypass that attachment gate. Select the state-dependent response, clear movement/attachment/projectile state and queue audio.
; Only enter once while the player is active. Select failure animation, stop normal street systems,
; hide attachment sprites, reset objects and queue the failure sound.

; Player handler words, direction and animation lookups, motion pairs, tile properties, pointer arrays and variable-width animation records. Existing player consumers anchor named starts; the $8d1f..$8d70 zero run is retained as data. Original complete subtable segmentation is unresolved.
; Preserve registers, select CHR bank 0, upload palette/OAM and pending background strips. Read
; controllers and toggle pause on a fresh Start edge. Run collision, scrolling, object, HUD and timer
; updates, perform the raster split, then restore registers. Audio is partly deferred to mainline.
; Upload the 64-byte tile strip in reverse buffer order to the current PPU address.
; Y selects an eight-byte slice of the attribute shadow; stream it to PPUDATA and mark background
; transfer work performed.
; Mask held input with the shared button mask and update a dedicated latch. Return A=1 only for a changed nonzero masked value; otherwise A=0. No live caller has been identified.
; Mask the controller with the Start bit and compare with the prior sample. Return A=1 only on a newly
; held press, otherwise zero.
; Latch controller ports and read eight serial bits. Merge the two sampled bit streams into
; ControllerHeld; the exact peripheral interpretation of the second bit is not established.
; When enabled and unpaused, shift the camera history and subtract current speed with nametable wrap.
; On a new 16-pixel boundary upload prepared tile/attribute strips, advance the route row and stop at
; the configured street extent.
; Apply the delayed camera position to PPUSCROLL and choose the vertical nametable bit in the PPUCTRL
; shadow.
; On a changed route row, read four selectors from the route stream. Select geometry, random tile,
; spawn and object descriptor lists, then build tile/attribute strips for both nametables.
; Walk two-byte row decoration records until $ff. Matching rows select one of four random variants;
; skip reserved variants $14/$15, patch both strips and request upload.
; Resolve the selected decoration through its pointer table. Set the one-cell geometry and patch the
; tile and attribute shadows for both nametable destinations.
; Resolve a layout-size offset into the metatile record and copy its two tile rows into the reversed
; 64-byte strip buffer. Width and orientation are supplied in scratch fields.
; Preserve unrelated quadrants in the attribute shadow. Extract each packed two-bit palette, shift it
; into the destination quadrant and advance source groups every four cells.
; Use the 14-position row cycle to derive tile and attribute PPU addresses for two strips. Also
; compute attribute shadow offsets and quadrant parity.
; Unsigned shift/add multiply: byte $12 times byte $13 produces the word $14/$15. $13/$16 become the
; shifted multiplicand; inputs are destroyed.
; Blank two nametables, clear strip shadows and hide OAM. Select stage-dependent
; graphics/palette/speed, initialize timers and camera, and choose the route stream from StageIndex.
; Stage >= $0a changes the random-selection mask.
; Stream sixteen palette-shadow bytes to $3f00, then restore the palette address latch.
; A is the tile for sprite zero at X=0,Y=$ca. The marker supports the sprite-zero-hit raster split.
; Set four bottom-edge sprites with the same tile and eight-pixel X spacing. Used alongside the raster
; marker during initialization.
; Repeated numeric lookup ramps, descending little-endian coordinate pairs, zero runs and display
; records between independently established code endpoints. Indexed consumers and nearby routines
; checked; precise original segmentation remains unresolved.
; A selects a story/result card. Disable rendering, decode its display, install CardNmi and fade in.
; Timed waits can be shortened by Start or the tested action button; card 9 has special input handling
; and card 12 sets an additional completion latch.
; Preserve registers, wait briefly, update shared animation/HUD/audio and controllers, decrement
; FrameDelay, reset scroll and return from NMI.
; Wait for sprite-zero hit, then use deliberately timed dummy reads/NOPs around palette changes.
; Switch CHR bank 1 and PPU pattern selection for the lower display. Preserve timing instructions and
; addressing modes.
; Select HUD graphics, initialize its dirty flags and palette, install attribute bytes and draw the
; first queued field.
; Scan seven dirty flags in reverse order and draw one field. Descriptors hold PPU address and mode;
; text mode remaps ASCII punctuation/digits/letters, raw mode streams bytes until zero. A zero
; descriptor byte redirects to another pointer.
; Add three decimal bonus digits into the low score digits, propagate decimal carry through all six
; ASCII digits and mark score dirty. Carry from each subtraction deliberately feeds the next digit.
; Compare six ASCII score digits lexicographically against high score and next-life threshold. Update
; high score if larger; crossing the threshold awards one life capped at nine and raises the threshold
; Subtract a fractional stage-dependent rate from a 16-bit accumulator. On borrow, decrement three
; ASCII time digits with decimal correction. At zero stop timer systems and trigger player failure
; when appropriate.
; Refresh the meter palette and copy 32 bytes of palette shadow into its saved copy.
; While enabled, unpaused and before stage $0c, subtract the configured rate from a three-byte meter.
; Clamp at zero, trigger failure if active, otherwise refresh the meter palette.
; Map the rounded high meter bytes to three palette segments. Full segments use a fixed color pair; a
; partial segment uses the top three bits of the rounded middle meter byte; remaining segments are empty.
; X selects a color-pair entry; Y selects its position in the lower-display palette shadow.
; Restore the meter to three units and reload its initial palette colors.

; Input A is a small unsigned increment with no byte overflow. Return the unsaturated sum in A below three without storing it. At saturation store high=3, clear both fraction bytes and return A=0. No live caller is established.
; A supplies the high meter byte; clear its two fractional bytes.
; Intentional repeated indirect reads consume time during palette writes. Register values and exact
; instruction timing are part of the raster sequence; these are not ordinary data fetches.
; MeterPartialColorPairOffsets supplies eight even byte offsets from the rounded middle byte >> 5.
; MeterSegmentPaletteOffsets supplies the three shadow destinations. MeterColorPairs has nine
; two-byte colors (empty offset 0, full offset 16); partial segments select offsets 0..14.
; Neighboring palette/display records remain grouped; original full segmentation is unresolved.
; Draw the accumulated route, install RouteNmi, initialize the blinking choice and wait for
; confirmation. Fade out and disable rendering on exit.
; Decode the map display, hide OAM and walk route-history bytes. Marker $04 is followed by a PPU
; address; other bytes select two route tiles and a marker sprite.
; Show both possible branches once, then start the selected choice blinking with a 15-frame interval.
; Upload route OAM, process route input and blink, reset scroll, update shared
; animation/controllers/audio and FrameDelay, then restore registers.
; While selection is active, confirm with Start/action or test directional input. Toggle the displayed
; choice every fifteen frames.
; Look up the alternate branch direction. Change selection only if the corresponding direction is held
; and the two branches differ; special direction codes are rejected.
; Append the chosen direction to route history and resolve StageIndex plus the post-street mode
; selector from parallel tables.
; Convert the current PPU tile address to an eight-pixel sprite position. Append a marker tile to the
; OAM shadow and advance its sprite index.
; Select the branch from route node and choice. Special codes swap the selected side or suppress
; drawing; otherwise write the on/off choice tile at its PPU destination.
; Add the direction-indexed signed PPU displacement to the route cursor and update PPUADDR.
; Set PPUADDR to the direction-indexed displacement from the route cursor without changing that
; cursor.
; Create an initial $04/address marker in the route history and reset the route node.
; Save history length, mode and route node before advancing the route.
; Restore history length, mode and node after a failed bonus so the preceding route can be retried.
; Save the retry checkpoint and commit the new route item. Negative mode selectors add a
; marker/address record and select the next route node.
; Map progression records, paired stage selectors, little-endian stage-layout addresses consumed by
; $94D8, low-valued tile-layout records and repeated encoded graphics data. Entire interval inspected,
; no code candidates conflict; exact subtable formats not all established.
; X selects source/destination PPU addresses in parallel tables. Select CHR bank 1, then decode the
; display stream stored in CHR-backed PPU space.
; Read packet headers through buffered PPUDATA. Zero ends; positive counts copy literal bytes;
; negative counts repeat the next byte count&$7f times. Track source and destination PPU addresses
; independently across page carries. Rendering must be disabled.
; Repeated VRAM address pairs and bounded pointer words between established code endpoints; no code
; interpretation asserted.
; When object updates are enabled and unpaused, process player collisions, consume both row spawn
; lists and run the ten-slot object pool.
; Skip collision during a background rebuild. For visible objects, derive a rectangle from type
; metadata and test it against the player rectangle. Dispatch enabled collisions through the type
; table.
; Walk two-byte row spawn records until a negative terminator. On the matching route row, find a free
; slot and initialize a script placeholder. Periodically vary the spawned script according to
; movement/equipment state.
; Resolve a four-variant script/position set for each matching row record. Choose a random variant
; under the stage mask, skip reserved type $15 and initialize a free slot.
; Scan ten slots in reverse. A type of $ff is free. Count down script delay; at zero fetch an opcode
; and jump through the object-script handler table. Optional behavior selects another indirect handler
; before physics.
; Y is the script cursor. Fetch the opcode, double it into the handler table and tail-dispatch with
; the current slot retained in scratch.
; An optional per-object behavior selector chooses a movement handler; otherwise integrate normal
; physics.
; Integrate signed acceleration into two fixed-point velocity pairs, clamp horizontal/vertical speeds,
; add velocity to multi-byte positions and compensate for delayed camera motion. Then project the
; object into OAM and resume the slot scan.
; Test four rectangle corners against the visible bounds. Objects with no visible corner are retired
; after first appearing. Resolve type-specific sprite offsets/count, then write each allocated OAM
; position; hide out-of-range Y values.
; Search backward through the OAM ownership map for a free $ff entry, claim it for the current object
; and save the remaining search cursor. Caller guarantees enough free slots; no exhaustion bound is
; present here.
; Search backward for the current object owner and convert the ownership index to an OAM byte offset.
; The first eight OAM sprites are reserved for other systems.
; Hide every sprite owned by the current object, free its OAM entries and mark the object slot $ff.
; Mark ten object slots and 52 OAM ownership entries free, hide their sprites and reset spawn
; counters.
; Compare two unsigned rectangles in scratch $9a..$a1. Test both relative-axis orderings; return A=1
; on overlap or touching edges, A=0 on separation. Callers prefilter coordinate overflow.
; Set the signs of the object acceleration components from its position relative to the player. The
; stage supplies the acceleration magnitude, then normal physics resumes.
; Choose horizontal sign and vertical flag from object/player position comparisons, clear behavior and resume integration.
; Index spawn parameters by twice-delayed scroll speed, choose a signed random X jitter of magnitude 0..31, then clear behavior. Script $0c selects an alternate X lookup.
; Read one tile per owned sprite followed by a duration byte. Update the script cursor and continue
; through behavior/physics.
; Read one attribute byte per owned sprite, then advance the script cursor and dispatch the next
; command.
; Read a script-relative low-byte target, subtract the script base low byte and replace the cursor.
; This encoding relies on its script-page contract.
; Set object type, allocate its required sprite slots, advance past opcode/argument and dispatch the
; next script command.
; Read X/Y integer velocity and acceleration, clear fractional velocity bytes and continue script
; dispatch.
; Read a behavior selector, save the next cursor and resume script dispatch.
; Consume the loop count into the current slot and continue at the next command.
; Decrement the per-slot count; loop to the encoded low-address cursor while nonzero, otherwise skip the target operand.
; Only a visible parent can spawn. Apply the stage probability and a two-child cap, find a free object
; slot, clone the parent position and initialize the child script.
; Read a duration, advance the cursor and resume behavior/physics while the delay counts down.
; Combine horizontal/vertical acceleration signs into a direction mask, look up a script address low byte and store its relative cursor.
; Consume one attribute byte per owned sprite using the shape count and existing OAM-offset helper; preserve the final script cursor.
; Hold the command with a one-tick delay until the per-slot gate is enabled and object Y reaches the payload threshold; then skip the operand and redispatch.
; Remove the current object and return to the pool scan without advancing a removed script.
; Consume one audio command byte and immediately continue script dispatch.
; Reset the driving palette timer and enable its two update latches, then continue after this command.
; Consume the per-slot collision flag and continue dispatch.
; Ignore while raised. Retire the pickup, queue its sound, replenish the meter up to three units,
; increment the two ASCII pickup digits and add fifty score points. Decimal overflow restores the
; meter.
; Save the slot; unless the player is attached, remove this object, set equipment selector 2 and queue pickup audio.
; Unless attached, remove the pickup, enable the projectile subsystem, reset its state and add ten to the shared reward counter.
; Force the common player hit transition, restore the object slot and continue the collision scan.
; This separately dispatched response has the same forced-player-hit mechanics as the preceding response.
; This separately dispatched response also forces the shared player hit transition; its game distinction remains unresolved.
; Force the player response, restore the slot, then restart this object with script 9.
; Force the player response and restart this object with script 10.
; Force the player response and restart this object with script 11.
; Disable further collisions for this object and subtract $32 from car speed, applying the original unsigned comparison floor of $1e.
; Clear the success latch and collision flag. Speed at least $58 enables success and attempts to allocate a script-$10 object at the car position; full pool leaves allocation undone.
; Restore the saved slot and resume the collision scan.
; Select the ordinary rather than forced player response, restore the slot and continue the scan.
; Input A selects a new script for slot X. Reset its cursor and arm the one-tick dispatch delay; return to caller.

; Object handler/pointer arrays, signed sprite-coordinate and rectangle records, per-type sprite counts and animation pointers, followed by script/spawn records. Pool projection, collision and script consumers anchor the known table starts. Original record ownership and some payload boundaries remain unresolved; do not treat these bytes as CPU instructions.
; Tail of unresolved mixed interval localized: repeated FF-delimited short low-value records followed
; by repeated small-value lookup arrays, ending exactly at established routine 0x3b32. Preceding
; pointer words and following code inspected; no conflicting code candidates. Original table
; segmentation and meaning unresolved.
; When the projectile subsystem is enabled and unpaused, test firing input, object collisions, tile
; response and candidate probe positions.
; Action input launches only when equipped and no shot is active. Start near the player with signed
; upward velocity; clear the probe-ready latch and queue a sound.
; When probes are stable, compare the seven-pixel projectile rectangle with each visible object.
; Dispatch hit responses through a type-indexed table.
; Compute the next projectile position. Overflow clears the shot. Otherwise derive four PPU tile
; addresses using the same camera/nametable wrap as the player.
; Clear its active latch and hide the projectile sprite when the street display is active.
; Save the object slot, remove object and projectile, queue hit audio and resume the object-hit scan.
; Separate response entry with the same remove/projectile/audio mechanics; type-specific meaning remains unresolved.
; Remove object and projectile without queuing this response family’s hit sound.
; Remove the hit object/projectile, initialize replacement variant 2, queue hit audio and restore the scan slot.
; Remove object/projectile and initialize replacement variant 0 before resuming the hit scan.
; Remove object/projectile and initialize replacement variant 1 before resuming the hit scan.
; Separate type response with replacement variant 1 and hit audio.
; Remove object/projectile, shift the replacement X by $18, initialize variant 1 and resume the scan.
; Resume the object-hit scan without changing this object.
; Remove object/projectile, initialize replacement variant 2 and restore the scan slot.
; Choose corner order from vertical velocity sign, inspect the four buffered tile properties and
; dispatch any response. With no response, commit velocity and write the projectile sprite.
; Apply signed two-byte velocity to the projectile Y coordinate and write its position, fixed tile and
; attributes to OAM.
; Input A=0..2 selects parallel three-byte script/reward lookups. Reuse the saved slot, reset cursor/type sentinel, award the selected hundreds value through the score helper and return.

; Two parallel three-byte lookups indexed by replacement variant A=0..2: script selector at $bdf4, score hundreds at $bdf7. The following code restarts at $bdfa; these six bytes are not part of that instruction stream.
; Clear the projectile, queue tile-hit audio and return to the tile collision caller.
; Tail back to the existing projectile tile-scan continuation.

; Projectile tile-handler words, corner offsets, two order-list pointers/lists and object-hit handler words. Existing four-corner scans and hit dispatch explain consumers; exact original table segmentation beyond established starts is not asserted.
; Initialize cafe, enable its NMI and wait until its activity latch clears or the hit counter reaches
; 99. Convert the result to one/two/five hundreds, count that award into score and require at least
; fifty hits for success.
; Hide OAM, load the CHR-backed motion path and cafe/HUD displays. Initialize six incoming actors,
; projectile supply, selected lane and bonus counters, then draw the player.
; Pair each incoming lane actor with its returning projectile. A rectangle hit changes actor
; animation, removes the projectile and replenishes supply; eligible hits increment the counter and
; score.
; Convert the binary hit count to two digits by repeated subtraction and draw them in the upper-right
; OAM slots.
; When the moving special target shares the selected lane, test its rectangle against the player. A
; hit sets the failure latch, removes the target and restores one projectile.
; Count down spawn delay, choose a random free lane and reject overcrowded neighboring lanes. Periodic
; remaining-count thresholds spawn a special actor; later waves shorten the delay.
; Walk six active lane actors. Run shared animation, integrate movement and project each composite
; sprite into its lane OAM allocation.
; Integrate signed quarter-byte motion along each axis. At a lane threshold change animation or begin
; cafe failure; actors leaving the left edge retire. Preserve fractional motion in the paired fields.
; First missed actor stops new spawns, selects its failure animation and converts other live actors to
; retreat states. Subsequent calls leave the first failure selection intact.
; Walk the six returning lane projectiles, animate and move each left, then draw surviving sprites.
; Subtract horizontal speed; underflow frees the actor, hides its sprite and returns one supply unit.
; Advance the special target along a CHR-derived path, using a lane-dependent bound and Y base. Hide
; it and clear its active latch at the path end.
; Move the player between six lanes until the destination coordinate matches. While stable and not
; failing, Up/Down select a lane and Action launches a projectile if supply and slot permit.
; Run the shared animation and draw the player composite into the fixed player OAM allocation.
; Free the actor and hide its four sprites. Reduce future spawn delay by eight, clamped to thirty
; frames.
; Count down the temporary supply marker. Matching the current lane before expiration returns one unit
; and hides its sprite.
; Detect a fresh secondary-button edge. Spend one special charge, clear eligible lane actors with
; score awards, queue its sound and start a brief effect timer.
; Add one hundred score points through the shared decimal score helper.
; Upload cafe palettes and OAM, update cafe collisions/spawns/actors/input while active and unpaused,
; read controllers and toggle pause. Draw the hit counter, service fades, perform the raster split and
; tick frame/effect timers.
; Repeated four-byte NES palette groups and small display records between independently established
; code endpoints.
; Initialize school and wait for activity to end or 198 counter units. One displayed hit is two
; internal units; halve the counter for the fifty-hit success threshold and the result award.
; Load school/HUD displays, initialize the seven-lane player and moving spawner, clear counters and
; draw the starting player. Actors use the common bonus animation system.
; Walk fourteen actors, run animation, integrate their horizontal approach and draw them into fixed
; OAM allocations.
; Subtract the signed animation speed scaled by eight from the fixed-point horizontal position.
; Crossing the per-slot boundary enters the school miss handler.
; A missed live type $29 becomes failure animation $2c, stops spawning and converts all remaining $29
; actors to retreat state $2b.
; Interpolate the selected lane by opposing fractional coordinate changes. At a stable lane, Up/Down
; choose a neighbor within seven positions unless failure is active.
; Animate and draw the player from bonus slot fifteen at the fixed player OAM allocation.
; Animate bonus slot fourteen, update its sweep path, derive screen coordinates from the path state
; and project its composite sprite.
; Test each eligible incoming actor against player slot fifteen. On overlap queue the hit sound,
; increment the score/counter and convert the actor to its retreat animation.
; Integrate two opposing fixed-point path coordinates, with rate increasing per 64 hits. At tile
; boundaries try to spawn an actor. Clamp/reverse at either endpoint; a random decision near the
; center can also reverse direction.
; Clamp path coordinates to the far endpoint, clear fractions and select the returning spawner
; animation.
; Clamp path coordinates to the near endpoint, clear fractions and select the outgoing spawner
; animation.
; X is a path-derived slot. If spawning is enabled and it is free, choose an approach rate from score
; progression, initialize positions/animation and decrement remaining actors.
; Increment the school counter and award one hundred score points. Counter units are halved for the
; result display.
; Mark actor X animation inactive and hide its first owned OAM sprite through the actor-indexed offset lookup.
; Add one hundred score points using the common ASCII score accumulator.
; Halve the internal counter, convert to tens/units and draw two digits in the upper-right OAM slots.
; Upload palettes/OAM, run school collisions/actors/player/spawner while active and unpaused, read
; input and toggle pause. Draw hit digits, update fade channels and perform the raster split before
; returning.
; Repeated four-byte NES palette groups and small display records between independently established
; code endpoints.
; Initialize dance, enable shared meter/timer drains and wait until activity or time expires. Stop
; actors and either show the remaining-time award on success or clear movement rewards on failure.
; Load a CHR-backed motion path, palettes and dance display. Initialize three fixed actors and the
; player/partner pair, timer/meter rates, selector state and progress fields.
; Compare four active incoming actors with player slot four and partner slot seven. Player collisions
; reduce the progress accumulator and change animation; partner collisions award score.
; Choose a free slot and a weighted random starting path index. Initialize its animation, horizontal
; position and CHR-path Y coordinate; reset the spawn countdown.
; Walk four active incoming actors, run shared animation, advance along the motion path and project
; their sprites.
; Animate and project bonus slot five into its fixed OAM allocation.
; Animate and project bonus slot six into its fixed OAM allocation.
; If bonus slot eight is active, animate and project its ending/effect sprite group.
; Advance X and the modulo-64 path cursor by signed animation speed; derive Y from the CHR-loaded path
; table.
; Respect a short input repeat delay. Left/Right choose one of two orientations; Up/Down choose among
; three poses. A changed selector switches player and partner animations through parallel tables.
; Animate/project player slot four. Advance the partner slot seven animation using the same fixed OAM
